svg.title: The patch gap in Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report
svg.desc: Two panels drawn from Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report. Top panel, on a logarithmic time axis from one hour to sixty days: the median time from a vulnerability being discovered in the wild to being weaponized is now well below 24 hours, while Microsoft estimates enterprise remediation of critical external vulnerabilities takes 30 to 60 days; the space between is the exposure window. Bottom panel: phishing was the entry vector for 23 percent of intrusions Microsoft's incident responders investigated from July 2025 to June 2026, up from 7 percent a year earlier. Footer: in a test against an emulated enterprise with no defenders, Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5 each completed a 32-step attack chain to full domain compromise, the first models Microsoft saw do this autonomously.
svg.text: The patch gap: attackers in hours, defenders in weeks
Microsoft 2026 Digital Defense Report (published Oct 1–2, 2026). Figures are Microsoft's own; time axis is logarithmic.
Time to act on a newly exploited vulnerability
Share of investigated intrusions that began with phishing
Bar length proportional to share (20 px per percentage point).
First fully autonomous domain takeover in Microsoft's testing: Mythos and GPT-5.5, 32 steps, emulated enterprise, no defenders.
Microsoft also expects a multi-year spike in known-but-unpatched vulnerabilities, and says it has seen state actors experiment with
agentic AI, though "not yet observed at scale." Sources: Microsoft 2026 DDR; BleepingComputer; Help Net Security.
